comparison: Both bars place the field after the reported counterexample at the boundary of its mechanism. The Opus bar names, as a sharp version of the characterisation problem, whether the double-cover parity mechanism is necessary for failure within a named class; both bars name biregular and symmetric patterns, where the colour-refinement pinning of the manuscript (Proposition 2.1(4), Lemma 3.4) cannot apply, and graphs with degree-2 vertices (Conlon, Kim, Lee and Lee, Problem 1.5). The two selected candidates each remove one ingredient of the construction. candidate-girth-six asks about bipartite graphs without 4-cycles. There no point pair lies in two faces, so, as this record reads Equation (3.4), the construction's only correction term is absent. The class contains every 1-subdivision of a graph and every incidence graph of a linear hypergraph, and its smallest concrete test is the 1-subdivision of the counterexample (101 vertices, girth 8), whose density is t(H, W composed with W). candidate-biregular asks about biregular bipartite graphs. There colour refinement never becomes discrete, so the pinning step cannot apply, and every weakly norming graph lies in this class (Hatami); its smallest open case, K_{5,5} minus C_{10}, is named by Hatami and by Conlon and Lee. For both, either answer is informative: a proof gives a structural sufficient condition that the reported construction cannot violate, and a counterexample needs a mechanism other than the reported one. The failure signals differ: for girth-six, a deficit produced by 6-cycles (three faces meeting pairwise in distinct points); for biregular, a symmetric replacement for the type-pinning step. The resource demand is similar: both rest on decisive readings that the record holds (the manuscript, Conlon, Kim, Lee and Lee, Conlon and Lee 2017 and 2021, Hatami, Lee and Schulke) and on bounded attempts. candidate-edge-transitive is contained in candidate-biregular, candidate-subdivisions in candidate-girth-six, and candidate-small-spheres adds no mechanism. candidate-sidorenko-forcing and candidate-knrs-counterexample wait for decisive readings that the record has not done.
